questions.question: Who has been signed on as a brand ambassador of lubricant manufacturer Gulf Oil India in October 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Smriti Mandhana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Smriti Mandhana, an Indian cricketer**, has agreed to serve as a **brand ambassador for Gulf Oil India,** a producer of **lubricants**.
 
• As an **ambassador** for the firm, the **India women's vice-captain **joins current men's cricket star** Hardik Pandya **and **former captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni.**
 
• In addition to recognising the accomplishments of **Indian women cricketers**, **Gulf Oil** claimed that it hopes to "**celebrate women power**" and "inspire female audiences in the country" with the **cooperation**.
 
• Through this partnership,** Gulf Oil** claims to be the first lubricant company to name a female cricket player as an **ambassador** to represent the group and its culture. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gulf Oil India **

 
 
• ​**Gulf Oil** is aware that the dynamics of the automobile industry have changed, with more women now having a significant part in the choice to buy a vehicle and in its ongoing maintenance.
 
• The organisation claims to have recognised the shifting consumer demographics with the inclusion of **Smriti Mandhana** to its** roster of ambassadors** and is dedicated to appeal to and serve the new evolving customer environment in the segment.

questions.question: The motion of the body moving along a circular path is an example of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is accelerated motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The rate at which an **object's velocity** with respect to time changes is referred to as **acceleration in mechanics.**
 
• A body travelling in a circle at a constant speed is said to be moving at an **accelerated** **rate** since its motion is uniform in** speed but not in velocity**, which can be expressed in **magnitude** and **direction as a vector quantity.**
 
• The item is said to be **accelerating** when the **magnitude remains constant** but the direction shifts in a **circular motion**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decelerated motion**

 
 
• ​A moving item might slow down or come to a stop as a result of **unbalanced forces**, reducing its speed. For instance, when a ball is thrown upward, it experiences both the upward applied force and the **downward gravitational force**.
 
 
 
• **Non-uniform motion**
 
 
• ​No matter how long the time intervals are, **non-uniform motion **refers to movement in which the item does not go the same lengths in the same amount of time. The motion of the body is regarded as **non-uniform motion** whenever the **velocity** of the moving object changes at a different pace, throughout the course of the same time interval.
 
 
 
• **Uniform motion**
 
 
• This kind of motion is described as the **movement** of an item that travels in a straight line and maintains a **constant speed** along that line while traversing equal distances in similar amounts of time, regardless of the length of the time. If a body is **moving rectilinearly** and the motion is steady, then the** body's acceleration** must be zero.

questions.question: Which of the following bills can be initiated only in the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a Money bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Parliament's** ability to control how public funds are used is a crucial role.
 
• **Money Bills **provide the **government** access to **public funds.**
 
• Only on the **President's** suggestion may a **Money Bill **be tabled in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• **The Constitution's Article 110 **addresses money bills. **Rajya Parliament **cannot hear the **Money Bill first.**
 
• If a bill only has measures pertaining to money, it is referred to
 
 
• taxation
 
• borrowing of money by the government
 
• expenditure from or receipt to the **Consolidated Fund of India.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **How money bill is passed -**

 
 
• Only on the** President's **advice may a **Money Bill** be tabled in the **Lok Sabha**.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** must approve it with a simple majority of all members who are present and voting.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** may then send it for recommendations, which the** Lok Sabha** may accept or reject as it sees fit. If such suggestions are not made within 14 days, **Parliament** will be assumed to have approved them.

questions.question: From which year did Sangeet Natak Akademi, New Delhi, institute the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar?

questions.question: Which of the following are food preservatives?

options.text: Salt, sodium nitrite, spices and vinegar
Formic acid, vinegar and methyl alcohol

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Salt, sodium nitrite, spices and vinegar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Food preservation techniques** include those that increase food's resistance to microbial growth and **slow fat oxidation.**
 
• **Decomposition and rancidification** are slowed down as a result.
 
• **Food preservatives include salt, sodium nitrite, spices, and vinegar.**
 
• Processes that prevent the **aesthetic deterioration of food**, such as the **enzymatic** browning reaction that occurs when apples are chopped during food preparation, may also be included in **food preservation.**
 
• **Food preservation** helps to reduce food waste, which is a crucial step in lowering production costs, boosting the effectiveness of food systems, **enhancing food security and nutrition, and promoting environmental sustainability. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It has been demonstrated that some traditional **food preservation techniques** use less energy and leave a smaller carbon footprint than more **contemporary techniques.**
 
• It is known that several** food preservation techniques **produce carcinogens.
 
• Meat that has been salted, cured, fermented, or smoked is considered processed meat by the** World Health Organization's International Agency for Research on Cancer to be "carcinogenic to humans" in 2015.**

• **Rama Swamy Annavarapu**

questions.question: Which of the following Chola ruler built a temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vijayalaya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Around the **ninth century AD, the Muttaraiyar**, a small main **dynasty**, ruled the **Kaveri delta.**
 
• They served the **Pallava kings of Kanchipuram** as their subjects.
 
• In the middle of the ninth century, **Vijayalaya**, a member of the ancient mainly **Chola family **from **Uraiyur**, conquered the delta from the **Muttaraiyar**.
 
• He created the town of **Thanjavur** as well as a shrine dedicated to **Nishumbhasudini**.
 
• The Chola empire was thought to have been founded by **Vijayalaya**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayalaya's** successors expanded the kingdom's borders by conquest, increasing its size and power.
 
• **Rajaraja** **I**, regarded as the most powerful Chola emperor, established control over the majority of the southern regions in 985 after ascending to the throne.
 
• **Rajendra I,** the son of **Rajaraja**, carried on his father's policies and even launched raids against the **Ganga valley, Sri Lanka**, and nations in** Southeast Asia** while building a navy to support these operations.

questions.question: Which of the following line separates Pakistan and Afghanistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Durand line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ethnic Pashtuns who reside on both sides of the border are split by the **Durand Line.**
 
• It separates** Afghanistan's northeastern, eastern, **and** southern** provinces from** Pakistan's northern **and **western **provinces of **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan, **and** Gilgit-Baltistan.**
 
• The **Durand Line **is a boundary between **Afghanistan and British India** that runs through tribal regions in the Hindu Kush and was established in 1893 to delineate their separate spheres of influence.
 
• Subsequently, it served to delineate the** Pakistani-Afghanistan border.**
 
• The** Afghanistan-Pakistan border, a 2,670-kilometer (1,660 mi) **international land border between** Afghanistan and Pakistan in South Asia,** is defined by the** Durand Line.**
 
• The eastern end reaches **China's border**, while the western end reaches **Iran's border.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Radcliffe Line** served as the dividing line between the areas of **British India's Punjab and Bengal** provinces that were in** India and Pakistan.**
 
• At the conclusion of the **Shimla Conference, Tibet **and** Great Britain** negotiated the **McMahon Line,** the border between **Tibet and Assam in British India **(October 1913–July 1914).
 
• **Sir Henry McMahon**, the leading British negotiator, is honoured with the **moniker McMahon Line.**

questions.question: Warren Hastings became the first Governor General of Bengal in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1773.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 1773, Hastings was elected as the first Governor-General.**
 
• **Warren Hastings FRS **was a **British colonial administrator** who held the positions of **first Governor of the Presidency of Fort William (Bengal)**, head of the **Supreme Council of Bengal,** and** first Governor-General of Bengal** from 6 December 1732 to 22 August 1818.
 
• The **British Empire in India** is said to have been founded by him and **Robert Clive**.
 
• He was a vigorous reformer and organiser.
 
• He commanded **East India Company** troops that fought a coalition of native governments and the **French from 1779 to 1784.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Governor-General**

 
 
• A** governor-general is the title of an office holder.**
 
• In the context of **governors-general and former British **colonies, governors-general are chosen to serve as viceroys in any sovereign state over which the **monarch** of a personal union does not typically rule personally.
 
• In the past, significant **colonial governments **or other regions controlled by **monarchies or republics**, such as **Japan in Korea and France in Indochina**, have nominated governors general.

questions.question: Who wrote the book titled 'Gift to Monotheism'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Gift to Monotheists"** was written by** Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1809** and translated into **Bengali**.
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** was an outstanding social reformer in India who supported monotheism and provided evidence for it in the old **Hindu texts.**
 
• Often referred to as the** founder of modern India** and the** father of the Indian Renaissance, Raja Ram Mohan Roy** lived from 1772 to 1833.
 
• He was given the** title "Raja" by Akbar II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekanand**

 
 
• ​**Swami Vivekananda**, whose real name was **Narendranath Datta**, was an Indian Hindu monk, philosopher, writer, and religious teacher. He was also **Ramakrishna's** most important pupil.
 
• He lived from 12 January 1863 to 4 July 1902. He is credited with promoting interfaith understanding and elevating **Hinduism** to the position of a significant international religion. He was a vital player in the introduction of **Vedanta** and **Yoga** to the **Western** **world**.
 
 
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati**
 
 
• **​Dayananda** **Saraswati**, an **Indian** philosopher and social reformer who founded the **Arya** **Samaj**, a Vedic dharma reform movement, lived from 12 February 1824 to 30 October 1883.
 
• In 1876, he was the first to make the plea for Swaraj as "**India for Indians**," which **Lokmanya** Tilak eventually embraced.
 
 
 
• **Kehsavchand Sen**
 
 
• **​Keshub** **Chandra** **Sen**, a Hindu philosopher and social reformer who lived from 19 November 1838 to 8 January 1884, made an effort to integrate **Christian theology** with **Hinduism**.
 
• He was a Hindu who was born in the** Bengal Presidency of British India **and joined the **Brahmo Samaj** in 1857 before starting his own breakaway group, the "**Bharatvarshiya Brahmo Samaj**," in 1866 while the **Brahmo Samaj** was still run by **Debendranath Tagore.**
 
 

70:T

questions.question: Yamini Krishnamurthy is famous for which dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mungara Yamini Krishnamurthy**, an **Indian dancer **who specialises in **Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam**, was born on December 20, 1940.
 
• In **Madras, Yamini Krishnamurthy** made his debut in 1957.
 
• She is honoured to serve as the **Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam's Asthana Nartaki** (resident dancer).
 
• She was also referred to as the "**torch bearer**" of the **Kuchipudi dancing style.**
 
• The **Padma Shree** (1968), **Padma Bhushan** (2001), and **Padma Vibhushan** (2016), three of the highest civilian honours bestowed by the **Republic of India**, were among the many honours she received for her dancing career.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri**

 
 
• **​**The state's official language is Meitei (also known as **Manipuri**). It is a recognised language of the **Republic** of India and is widely spoken in the **Manipur** region.
 
• Like most of **Northeast India, Manipur** has a significant amount of **linguistic** **diversity** in addition to Meitei.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• **​**A significant ancient Indian classical dance, known as **Odissi** or **Orissi** in older writings, has its roots in the temples of **Odisha**, an eastern coastal state of India.
 
• In the past, **Odissi** was primarily performed by women, and it used songs that were written and created in accordance with the ragas and talas of the music to express religious stories and spiritual ideals, notably those of **Vaishnavism**.
 
 
 
• **Yakshagana**
 
 
• ​In the districts of **Dakshina** **Kannada**, **Udupi, Uttara Kannada, Shimoga,** and the **western** portion of **Chikmagalur** in the state of **Karnataka**, as well as in **Kasaragod** district in the state of **Kerala**, **yakshagaana** is a traditional theatre that combines dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques in a distinctive style and form.
 
• It is thought to have developed from pre-classical theatre and music during the **Bhakti** movement.
 
 

79:T

questions.question: What is the set of ecosystem called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Biome.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **biome** is the overall region of an **ecosystem**.
 
• A community of **plants and animals** that exist naturally in a place is referred to as a **biome**.
 
• These species share regional traits that are unique to that location.
 
• A **biome** is the** general ecological community**.
 
• There are three **types** of **biomes**: **marine, freshwater, and terrestrial.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stratosphere**

 
 
• ​ The** second layer of the Earth's atmosphere**, the **stratosphere**, is situated below the mesosphere and above the **troposphere**. The **stratosphere** is a layer of the **atmosphere** made up of stratified **temperature layers**, with warm layers of air high in the sky and cool layers of air low in the sky, not far from the **Earth's surface**.
 
 
 
• **Hydrosphere**
 
 
• The total mass of water present on, beneath, and above the surface of a planet, minor planet, or **natural satellite** is known as the **hydrosphere**. The **hydrosphere** on **Earth** has been present for nearly 4 billion years, yet it is still evolving.
 
 
 
• **Atmosphere**
 
 
• **A layer** (or layers) of gases that surround a planet and are held in place by the gravity of the** planetary body** is known as an **atmosphere**. When **gravity** is strong and the **temperature** of the **atmosphere is low,** a planet preserves its **atmosphere**.

questions.question: Who choreographed the Bollywood song 'Mohe Rang Do Laal' from Bajirao Mastani?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Birju Maharaj.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Bollywood song "**Mohe Rang Do Laal**" from **Bajirao Mastani** was choreographed by **Birju Maharaj.**
 
• He was honoured with the **Filmfare Award for Best Choreography in 2016** for his work on **Deepika Padukone's performance in Bajirao Mastani.**
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj**, an Indian dancer, composer, vocalist, and representative of the Lucknow "**Kalka-Bindadin**" Gharana of Kathak dance, lived from 4 February 1938 to 16 January 2022.
 
• He was a member of the **Maharaj family of Kathak dancers,** which included his father and master, **Acchan Maharaj**, as well as his two uncles, **Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj.**
 
• He was a vocalist and also studied **Hindustani classical music**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bajirao Mastani**

 
 
• **​Sanjay Leela Bhansali** is the director of the 2015 Indian epic historical romance film** Bajirao Mastani.**
 
• He also co-produced the movie alongside **Eros International **and wrote the **soundtrack**.
 
• In addition to Tanvi Azmi, Vaibhav Tatwawaadi, Milind Soman, Mahesh Manjrekar, and Priyanka Chopra, the movie also stars Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone, and Priyanka Chopra in supporting parts.
 
• The **Maratha Peshwa Bajirao I (1700–1740 AD) **and his **second wife, Mastani**, are the subjects of the **Marathi novel Rau by Nagnath S. Inamdar**, which served as the basis for the film** Bajirao Mastani.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a strong reducing agent used to reduce aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acid chlorides, carboxylic acids and even carboxylate salts to alcohols?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lithium aluminium hydride.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **LiAlH₄** is a **potent**, unselective reducer of polar double bonds that is most often considered to be an** H⁻ source. Aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acid chlorides, carboxylic acids,** and even **carboxylate** **salts** will all be converted to **alcohols via this process**.
 
• Often referred to as **LAH, lithium aluminium hydride** is an** inorganic substance** with the **chemical formula Li[AlH₄] or LiAlH₄.**
 
• It is a white solid that was found in 1947 by** Finholt, Bond, and Schlesinger**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Titanium hydride**

 
 
• ​In most cases, the term **"titanium hydride" **refers to the **inorganic substance TiH₂** and related **nonstoichiometric substances**. In addition to being utilised as an additive in the creation of **Alnico** sintered magnets, metal foam, powdered titanium metal, and pyrotechnics, it is commercially accessible as a stable grey/black powder.
 
 
 
• **Calcium hydride**
 
 
• **Calcium hydride**, often known as **alkaline earth hydride**, is a **chemical compound** having the formula **CaH2**. This grey powder reacts violently with water to release **hydrogen gas** (white if pure, which is uncommon). **CaH₂** is thus employed as a desiccant or **drying agent**. **CaH2 is a saline hydride**, which means that it has a salt-like structure.
 
 
 
• **Bismuth hydride**
 
 
• ​The **chemical compound** known as **bismuthine** has the formula **BiH₃**. **BiH₃**, the heaviest **analogue of ammonia** (**a pnictogen hydride**), is unstable and breaks down into **bismuth metal at temperatures **well below **zero degrees. **This compound has a **pyramidal structure as predicted, with H-Bi-H angles roughly 90 degrees.**
 
 

8c

questions.question: The headwaters of the river Ganga is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bhagirathi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gangotri Glacier feeds the "Bhagirathi," Ganga's headwaters.**
 
• At **Devaprayag in Uttarakhand,** the** Alaknanda joins it**.
 
• The **Ganga** leaves the mountains and enters the plains in **Haridwar**.
 
• A number of significant rivers, including the **Yamuna, the Ghaghara, the Gandak, and the Kosi,** join the **Ganga** from the **Himalayas**.
 
• The **Ganges** is thought to have its origins in the **Bhagirathi in Hindu mythology and culture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mandakini**

 
 
• ​In the **Indian state of Uttarakhand**, the** Mandakini River** is a** tributary of the Alaknanda River**.
 
• The river emerges from the **Chorabari** **Glacier** and flows for around 81 kilometres (50 miles) between the **Rudraprayag and Sonprayag regions.**
 
• The river passes past the Hindu shrine **Madhyamaheshwar** at **Ukhimath** before joining the river** Songanga at Sonprayag.**
 
 
 
• **Alaknanda**
 
 
• ​The **Alaknanda** is one of the **two headstreams of the Ganges**, the principal river of Northern India and the holy river of Hinduism.
 
• It originates in the **Himalayas** and flows through the** Indian state of Uttarakhand.**
 
• Due to its longer length and flow, the **Alaknanda** is regarded as the **Ganges**' source stream in hydrology; yet, in Hindu tradition and culture, the **Bhagirathi**, the other headstream, is regarded as the source stream.
 
 

96

questions.question: In hockey, what is the meaning of the signal if the umpire points both arms horizontally towards the goal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Penalty corner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If the **umpire raises both arms horizontally in the direction of the goal,** it is a **penalty corner **of the signal.
 
• A **defensive violation** within the **penalty circle** or a willful violation within the **defensive 23-meter zone** results in a **penalty corner** being issued.
 
• A **penalty corner**, sometimes referred to as a short corner in field **hockey**, is a sanction imposed on the opposing side.
 
• **Attacking players** seek them out eagerly because they offer a great chance to score. **Players** learn specialised abilities for this phase of the game, such as the** drag flick,** and there are specific rules that only apply in **penalty corners.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hockey **

 
 
• ​The term "**hockey**" refers to a **group of different summer and winter team games** that were first played on an **outdoor field,** **a sheet of ice, or a dry floor,** like in a **gymnasium**. While the specific regulations, player counts, attire, and most notably the playing field differ amongst these games, they all include two opposing teams utilising sticks to direct a ball or disc towards a goal.
 
• **Hockey comes in a variety of forms**.
 
• Skates, whether wheeled or bladed, are used in some games yet not in others.
 
• The word "**hockey**" is frequently followed by another word, such as "f**ield hockey," "ice hockey," "roller hockey," "rink hockey," or "floor hockey,"** to assist distinguish between these different games.

questions.question: Government of India has appointed _______ ​as Controller General of Accounts in October 2022
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharati Das.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian government** has selected **Ms Bharati Das**, an **Indian Civil Accounts Service (ICAS)** officer from the 1988 batch, as the **department's controller general of accounts (CGA).**
 
• She has held significant positions in different **Central Ministries,** including the **Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Finance, Health, Home Affairs, and CBDT**.
 
• Before accepting the position of** Controller General of Accounts,** **Ms Bharati Das** held the position of **Pr. Chief Controller of Accounts (Pr. CCA) **in the Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Home Affairs, and later the **Central Board of Direct Taxes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Controller General of Accounts**

 
 
• The primary accounting advisor to the **GOI is the Controller General of Accounts (CGA).**
 
• The **Central and State Governments' debts, deposits, cash,** and other **financial activities** are all audited by him.
 
• The **CGA** specifies the form of accounts as well as the general accounting standards for the **federal and state governments.**

questions.question: Low annual range of temperature and high annual rainfall are characteristics of a _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is tropical humid climate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tropical humid regions have low yearly temperature variation and substantial annual rainfall.**
 
• The **climatic zone** known as the **humid tropics** is one in which **evapotranspiration** outpaces precipitation for at least 270 days out of every year and mean monthly **temperatures** are continuously high and exceed 18 C.
 
• The first of the five main climatic groups assigned the letter A in the** Köppen climate** classification is the **tropical climate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mediterranean climate **

 
 
• **Hot, dry summers and warm, rainy winters are characteristics of the Mediterranean climate**. **Central California, Central Chile**, and the coasts of **South Eastern** and **South Western Australia** all have a **Mediterranean climate**. 
 
• In the summer, **subtropical** highs affect these locations, and in the winter, westerly winds. Hence, the region experiences hot, dry summers and warm, rainy winters.**​**
 
 
 
• **Temperate climate**
 
 
• The region of the globe between the middle **latitudes**, or 40 to 60 degrees north-south of the **Equator**, is known as the **temperate zone**. The areas of the **Earth** between the tropics and the poles are known as the** temperate zones.**
 
• The **temperate climate** is the one that prevails in this area. These places' average yearly **temperatures** show that they are **neither extremely hot nor extremely cold.**
 
 
 
• **Cold climate**
 
 
• **Cold climates** are one of the types of climates on our list that affect locations that man has not inhabited, and plant and animal species hardly survive. The **arctic** **environment** is the most **extreme subtype **and is **inhospitable** to all life except for a few species of lichens and moss.
 
• **Polar and highland climates** are two examples of **chilly climates.**

questions.question: In ancient times, the area to the south of the Ganga was known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Magadha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The region south of the **Ganga** along these rivers was referred to as **Magadha** in the past. Its kings established a sizable realm and were extremely strong. There were also established kingdoms in other regions of the nation. 
 
• Before **Bihar** was expanded, **Magadha** was a **territory** and **one of the sixteen Mahajanapadas, or "Great Kingdoms,**" of the **Second Urbanization**, which occurred at the **eastern Ganges Plain between 600 and 200 BCE.**
 
• The **Ganga, Sone, and Champa rivers**, in that order, confined the original **Magadha kingdom's territory** to the north, west, and east, while the eastern spurs of the **Vindhya** **mountains** formed its southern border.

 [IMAGE: https://i.pinimg.com/474x/62/91/57/62915799c2928c33d102afa5774d9b04.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga**

 
 
• A **transnational river in Asia**, the **Ganges** passes through **Bangladesh and India**.
 
• The 2,704 km river has its source in the **Uttarakhand** region of **India's western Himalayas**.
 
• It receives the **Yamuna**, a **right-bank tributary** that rises in the **western Indian Mountains**, as well as many left-bank tributaries from **Nepal**, which account for the majority of its flow, as it runs south and east across the **Gangetic plain of North India.**
 
• **Rivers flow into the Ganga from both banks**. The **Yamuna and Son** are its tributaries on its right bank. While some left bank tributaries include the **Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi.**
 
• It is **India's largest river system.**

questions.question: _______ port, situated at the head of Gulf of Kuctch has been developed as a major port to cater to the needs of western and north-western parts of the country and also to reduce the pressure at Mumbai port.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kandla.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In order to serve the needs of the **western and northwestern regions of the country** and to relieve strain on **Mumbai port, Kandla Port**, located at the head of the **Gulf of Kuchchh,** has being constructed as a significant port.
 
• The port is specifically made to take in massive amounts of **fertiliser, fertiliser derivatives, and petroleum products.**
 
• To relieve the strain on the **Kandla port, the offshore terminal at Vadinar was built.**
 
• The** hinterland's border** cannot be precisely defined because it is not fixed in space.
 
• In the majority of circumstances, the **hinterlands of two ports may cross paths.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mumbai port trust**

 
 
• **​**The **Mumbai Port Trust** often referred to as the **Bombay Port Trust,** is a port located in the** middle of India's west coast **on the naturally deep-water harbour of **Mumbai (Bombay)**, which is located in the **Maharashtra state**. The **island metropolis of Mumbai** to the **west** and the **Konkani mainland** to the east and north provide protection for the 400 square kilometres (150 sq mi) harbour. The harbour faces the** Arabian Sea **and opens to the south.
 
• The **Mumbai Port Trust** (MbPT, originally the Bombay Port Trust (BPT)), an independent organisation completely owned by the **Government of India**, is responsible for managing the **port**.
 
• While most container traffic is sent to **Nhava Sheva port** across the harbour, the port is mostly used for **bulk goods**.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Citizenship Act passed by the Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1955.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Citizenship Act of 1955** was amended by the **Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA act)**, which was first introduced in** Lok Sabha in 2016.**
 
• **A Joint Parliamentary Committee** was given this act, and it later produced a report that was delivered on January 7, 2019.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** passed the **Citizenship Amendment Act** on January 8, 2019, but it expired with the dissolution of the **16th Lok Parliament.**
 
• **Amit Shah**, the minister of home affairs, reintroduced this bill on December 9 in the** 17th Lok Sabha**, and it was later approved on December 10.
 
• On December 11th, the** Rajya Sabha** also approved the **legislation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Citizenship Amendment Act**

 
 
• ​The Act aims to amend the **Citizenship Act of 1955** to offer **citizenship** to illegal immigrants from **Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan** who are **Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, and Christian** words, the Act aims to facilitate **Indian citizenship** for persecuted individuals from India's neighbouring nations.
 
• Those who were "forced or compelled to seek sanctuary in India due to persecution on the basis of religion" are covered by the law. It tries to safeguard these individuals from** illegal immigration processes.**
 
• For applicants who practise one of these six religions, the change reduces the naturalisation requirement from 11 to 5 years.
 
• The applicant must have arrived in India on or before December 31, 2014, which is the deadline for **citizenship**.
